mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 3 months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >25 bps over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises >25 bps over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 6% for two consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market tightening, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing sectors and drags S&P 500 returns lower over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls for two quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate to above 4.5% triggers a risk-off shift in financial markets, raising bond yields and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS jumps above 4.5% in one month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months signals labor market churning and instability, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >0.5% AND UNRATE rises >0.2pp over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS rises >0.5% and UNRATE rises >0.2pp over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) over four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts earnings for cyclical sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS rises for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) over two months signals a broad-based slowdown in supply-side activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both fall >1% over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST fall >1% over two months.
